title: Behaviour as a parameter
description:
Write in `solution.c`:

```c
void apply(int *values, size_t count, int (*f)(int));            /* values[i] = f(values[i]) */
size_t count_if(const int *values, size_t count, bool (*test)(int));
int negate(int x);
bool is_negative(int x);
int compare_ints(const void *a, const void *b);       /* for qsort: smallest first */
int compare_by_length(const void *a, const void *b);  /* for qsort on an array of const char *:
                                                         shorter first, equal lengths alphabetically */
```

The tests sort with `qsort(values, n, sizeof values[0], compare_ints)` and `qsort(words, n, sizeof words[0], compare_by_length)`. In the second, each element is a `const char *`, so the comparison receives **pointers to those pointers**.
hints: `compare_ints` must not return `x - y`: with the biggest and smallest ints in the test, the subtraction overflows. `(x > y) - (x < y)` gives -1, 0 or 1 safely.
